content.title: About
content.content: The sausage biscuit sandwich is a quick snack consisting of a grilled or boiled sausage placed between two halves of a soft biscuit (American style). It is often served hot, sometimes with mustard, ketchup or melted cheese.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the United States in the early 20th century as convenient street food.
Traditional biscuit for the sandwich is the American "biscuit", which is flaky and savory, not a sweet cookie.
It is sometimes called a "pull‑ap" when served in small bite‑size portions at buffets.
Variations include adding cheddar cheese, fried onions, or pickles.
In some regions turkey or chicken sausages are used for a lighter version.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: The sausage provides animal protein needed for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the biscuit and fats from the sausage delivers quick energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat products contain vitamin B12 and niacin, important for the nervous system and metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Sausage is a source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Calcium (when cheese is added)
items.content: If cheese is included, the sandwich gains calcium, beneficial for bone health.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Most ready‑made sausages contain a lot of salt, which can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Traditional sausages are rich in saturated fats, which in excess may contribute to cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Preservatives and nitrites
items.content: Some sausages contain nitrites that can form potentially harmful compounds when heated.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The biscuit is usually made from wheat flour, making the dish unsuitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of biscuit and sausage makes the sandwich calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich can be eaten hot, reheated in a microwave or skillet until the biscuit is golden. Add mustard, ketchup, mayo, or a slice of cheese if desired. For a lighter version use a whole‑grain biscuit and a turkey or chicken sausage.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Keep sausages and biscuits separate: sausages in their original packaging or tightly wrapped, biscuits in a dry place. When reheating, ensure the sausage reaches an internal temperature of at least 75 °C.
